chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Muhammad ibn Abdullah who said:

I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about a man who has a pasture (land/estate), and it has boundaries that reach twenty miles, and less or more. A man comes to him and says to him, 'Give me from the pasture of your estate, and I will give you such and such a dirham.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the estate is his, there is no problem.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on selling or leasing pasture land rights?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the permissibility (*ibahah*) of leasing private pasture lands (*dhiya'*) for a fixed monetary consideration, affirming individual property rights in agrarian transactions. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that ownership grants the proprietor the discretion to monetize usufruct rights, provided the land itself remains his property, a ruling foundational to Islamic commercial law (*fiqh al-mu'amalat*).
